summary: Round 1's blocking miss is fixed: Geno Smith is now the Jets quarterback in a 28-25 loss to Miami, which matches the brief. The rest of the claims I re-checked still trace, and the issue still reads as Boston Connor without hometown bias.

Used occasionally: “Who starts 165 yards over 287?” (lead); “What are you saving him for?” (recaps[5]). “I have questions.” (transactions) stays rare.

Wild takes in the calm of fact: “Superflex is a second quarterback slot, not a museum piece. … I don't make the rules.” (lead); “which is a lineup you delete.” (rankings[10]); “Start a chair.” (awards); “fifth is a gift.” (rankings[5]). All still read as opinion.
Two real outbursts: “FRAUD.” (lead) and “UNBELIEVABLE.” (recaps[3]). WELL! is the team name. No other ALL CAPS yelling.

Lead stays dry through Mahomes 19 of 33 for 165, Geno 23 of 30 for 287 in the Jets' 28-25 loss, and 113.72 to 116.60, then jumps to the museum-piece read and “FRAUD.” Recaps[3] goes from the Love/Doubs/Daniels lines to “Wild idea.” Recaps[6] lists Shrader, SF DEF, and Jones, then “pile of junk.”

Dismissive closes: “FRAUD.” (lead); “Start the skill players. It works.” (recaps[1]); “Worse bench.” (recaps[2]); “Wild idea.” (recaps[3]); “Bring a team next time.” (recaps[4]); “It was enough.” (recaps[6]); “Do that.” / “This is not a puzzle.” (awards)

Unpolished fan talk: “That's how you lose a week.” “From the couch” (rankings[4]); “pile of junk” (recaps[6]); “Gift-wrapped.” (waivers); “Unserious operation.” (rankings[4]); “a lineup you delete” (rankings[10])
Insults and slang: “FRAUD.”, “new disaster”, “pile of junk”, “lineup you delete”, “Unserious operation.” Profanity is left out this issue, which the guide allows as occasional.
Placed, not sprayed: “FRAUD.” (lead); “UNBELIEVABLE.” (recaps[3]); “The sponsor found a new disaster.” (recaps[5]). No carpet-bomb of bum/pathetic/embarrassing.

Comparisons that don't survive a second look: “not a museum piece” (lead); “Start a chair.” (awards); “One receiver covered a pile of junk.” (recaps[6]); “which is a lineup you delete.” (rankings[10])
No academic transitions or long metaphors: “About time.” “This was not a game.” “Bad draw. Worse bench.” “Gift-wrapped.” “Messy. Coin flip.” “museum piece” is a short fan jab, not an extended figure.

Questionable takes as law: “That's how you lose a week.” (lead); “I don't make the rules.” (lead); “They earned every inch of that drop.” (rankings[8]); “This is not a puzzle.” (awards); “Split, if they learned anything.” (preview)

Confident arguments that sag: yards-in as a Superflex statute (“I don't make the rules.”) (lead); “Ted Hurst caught zero balls on one target and they're third.” (rankings[3]); winning with Shrader at −1.00 treated as the method (recaps[6]); Daniels at −0.30 → “Start a chair.” (awards)

Craziest lines in a flat voice: “I don't make the rules. I just watch people ignore them.” (lead); “Start a chair.” (awards); “116.60 is a bad score. It was enough.” (recaps[6]); “which is a lineup you delete.” (rankings[10])

Dry swap math to “FRAUD.” (lead); recaps[3] opens already hot (“UNBELIEVABLE.”) then the zeros; recaps[5] goes from Pollard's 36.50 to “The sponsor found a new disaster.” Rankings[10] climbs from Love/Doubs/Daniels to “a lineup you delete.”

Detail, then a short insult: “FRAUD.” (lead); “It works.” (recaps[1]); “Worse bench.” (recaps[2]); “Wild idea.” (recaps[3]); “Bring a team next time.” (recaps[4]); “It was enough.” (recaps[6]); recaps[5] closes on the bench crime after the Noel roast

Defends the roast after the evidence cuts against it: Pollard 36.50 from the couch “and they still rose. … Unserious operation.” (rankings[4]); “You sat 36.50 and won anyway. … What are you saving him for?” (recaps[5]); “I would have started him out of spite.” after the 34.42 win (awards); “116.60 is a bad score. It was enough.” (recaps[6])

items.evidence: E1 is fixed: “Geno Smith went 23 of 30 for 287 yards and three scores in the Jets' 28-25 loss to Miami.” matches brief.json (Geno Smith, NYJ, opponent MIA, nfl_game “MIA 28, NYJ 25”) and the ESPN recap under that game. Cooper's bench line is now split: 22.50 vs bench 62.10. Superlatives (160.86 high, 90.70 low, 108.18 bench, 66.38 margin, 36.50 top player, +17.13 Elo bump) and the 14.60/17.48 derived swaps still match.

Irrational bits read as takes: “not a museum piece”, “I don't make the rules”, “FRAUD.”, “Start a chair.”, “lineup you delete.” ESPN-only claims are sourced: Chiefs' first loss; Love out a second week; Pollard's career-high-tying scores; Javonte's best rushing night; McCarthy's first start. No invented trades, firings, or quotes.

Straight carriers sit next to the jokes: “Mahomes went 19 of 33 for 165 yards in Kansas City's 20-3 loss at Seattle.” “Geno Smith went 23 of 30 for 287 yards and three scores in the Jets' 28-25 loss to Miami.” “Split lost 113.72 to 116.60. The margin was 2.88.” Injury notes and standout lines stay factual.
Caps twice in the issue (“FRAUD.”, “UNBELIEVABLE.”). No signature line repeated. “What are you saving him for?” appears once in recaps[5] (the award is a title).

Comic energy without hometown bias: short blunt openers, absurd reads (“museum piece”, “Start a chair.”), five-step lead and recaps, UC roasted as the sponsor. No Patriots/Fenway/“this state” framing; Maye, Stevenson, and CHI 30, NE 24 appear only as real box-score facts.

notes.quote: The sponsor found a new disaster. Left 36.50 and a 108.18 bench and still won.
notes.problem: The closer now lands on hammball's bench crime, which is what round 1 asked for, but the subject is dropped. The nearest noun is “the sponsor,” who did not sit 36.50, did not have a 108.18 bench, and did not win. The recap's opener and the 108.18 line make the intended subject recoverable; it is clumsy, not a stated falsehood.
notes.fix: Name hammball in the last sentence, or turn it into a real insult (“Sat the week's best player. Won anyway. Unserious.”) so the closer cannot be read as UC's line.
